replay_answer:
I would not grant Marcus 15% equity, CTO title, and governance rights on Friday. That package is too permanent before you know whether Marcus reduces dependency risk or becomes the dependency.

But Friday should not be a vague no or flat rejection. A vague later can trigger the disengagement risk you are trying to avoid. Make it a serious staged path: there may be a route to major upside and authority, but only after evidence.

The test is whether Marcus makes the company stronger beyond himself. Put a short evidence window around platform delivery, revenue relevance, client continuity, Jake and Lina/team dependence, knowledge transfer, and governance behavior.

Keep middle structures alive, but do not turn the conversation into a catalog. The useful distinction is not bonus versus full equity. It is commitment after proof versus irreversible commitment before proof.

Use exit math only as a warning about false precision. Until buyer assumptions, departure scenarios, and platform value are tested, the numbers should not carry the ownership decision.

Your Friday message can be: I want to explore a serious path with you, but I cannot grant irreversible ownership and governance rights before we prove what this partnership does to the company.
